AOC and Paris Hilton stood side by side at a press conference for the DEFIANCE Act, a bipartisan bill that would allow victims of sexually explicit deepfakes to sue those who created or distributed the AI images without consent. It would also establish a 10-year statute of limitations that begins either when the victim discovers the violation or turns 18.

The Senate unanimously passed the legislation in January, but the House has stalled it. Speaker Mike Johnson has not commented on why.

The legislation expands on the ‘Take It Down Act,’ which makes posting authentic and deepfake explicit imagery without consent a federal crime. It also requires social media companies and other websites to remove the imagery within 48 hours of a victim’s request.

Hilton appeared on Capitol Hill to appeal to the House as a survivor of a deepfake attack herself. When she was just 19 years old, an ex-boyfriend leaked more than 100,000 sexually explicit deepfake images of her online. She said the attack was deeply humiliating, and implored Congress to think of the young girls who don’t have the same resources she had.
